name: Central-Southern Persian Gypsy
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record cent2304 and its langdoc reference table (Moqaddam 1949; Wirth 1927; Sykes 1906; Sykes 1902).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; all four references typed 'wordlist_or_less' (Moqaddam: overview;wordlist).

sources.citation: Windfuhr, Gernot L. 2002 [updated 2012]. GYPSY ii. Gypsy Dialects. Encyclopaedia Iranica XI/4: 415-421 (online ed.).
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Lists this group under 'Central and Southern Persia': Ghorbati, endonym Il-e Fiuj, Arak area (Moqaddam, extensive data; Wirth); Ghorbati of Jiroft/Sirjan/Kerman (Sykes); Lori 'Mokki' of Baluchistan (Ivanow 1914, no linguistic data). States that most Iranian Gypsy dialects 'are based on local variants of Persian, having adopted both morphology and syntax'.

sources.citation: Ivanow, W. 1914. On the language of the Gypsies of Qainat (in Eastern Persia). JASB n.s. 10: 439-455.
sources.note: Only relevant line for this entry: footnote that 'the patois of Lori, or Gypsies of Baluchistan is still called Mokki' - no data on it. Its phonetics section and the remark 'Accentuation is not so strong as is Qaini' concern the Qainat jargon (casp1241), not cent2304.

sources.citation: de Goeje, M. J. [with J. Sampson]. 1907. Reviews: The Gypsies of Persia (Sykes 1902, 1906). Journal of the Gypsy Lore Society n.s. 1(2): 181-183.
sources.note: Nothing; identifies Romani cognates in Sykes's lists.

sources.citation: Sykes, P. Molesworth. 1906. The Gypsies of Persia: A Second Vocabulary. Journal of the Anthropological Institute of Great Britain and Ireland 36: 302-311 (note by M. L. Dames p. 311).
sources.note: Nothing. 96-item list for Jiruft, Sirjan and Khorasan; p. 302 'as every accent, etc., is given' refers to Persian-script vowel pointing by a 'good Persian scholar', not to word stress; Dames's note p. 311 is about g/k only.

sources.citation: de Goeje, M. J. 1903. Memoire sur les migrations des Tsiganes a travers l'Asie. Leiden: Brill (pp. 36-40 on the Persian Gypsies' language; comparative wordlist).
sources.note: Nothing; discusses only the sources of Persian Gypsy words (Ouseley, Newbold, Gobineau, Benjamin, Sykes) and etymologies.

sources.citation: Sykes, P. Molesworth. 1902. Anthropological Notes on Southern Persia. Journal of the Anthropological Institute of Great Britain and Ireland 32: 339-349 (section 'The Gypsies of Persia', pp. 344-349), with Dames, M. Longworth, Note on Major Sykes's Gypsy Vocabulary, pp. 350-352.
sources.note: Nothing. c. 100-word 'Gurbati' vocabulary from Kerman in Persian script + transliteration, no accent marks; Dames (p. 350) calls it 'an artificial secret dialect or jargon' whose 'grammar is based on Persian'.

sources.citation: Gobineau, Arthur de (communicated by A. F. Pott). 1857. Persische Studien. 1. Die Wanderstaemme Persiens. ZDMG 11: 689-699.
sources.note: Nothing found (poor Google scanned; grep for Betonung/Accent/Silbe/Aussprache gave no hits). Ethnonyms Kauli, Pessewan, 'zaban-e Kurbati' and a short vocabulary only.

sources.citation: Newbold, T. J. 1856. The Gypsies of Egypt [section 'The Gypsies of Persia', pp. 309-312]. Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society 16: 285-312.
sources.note: Nothing; Kaoli/Ghurbati vs Gaobaz ethnography and about ten secret words.
